title: Hamiltonian Simulation
summary: Approximate the evolution under a sum of terms with Trotter steps.
objectives: Implement one Trotter step for H = J Z⊗Z + h (X⊗I + I⊗X) with rzz and rx gates, and repeat it n times.
Choose the number of steps n so that the final state has fidelity at least 0.99 with the exact evolution.
Predict how the error of a first-order Trotter formula changes when n doubles.
mission: Simulate the evolution of two qubits under H = J Z⊗Z + h (X⊗I + I⊗X), with J = 1, h = 0.8 and time t = 2, starting in |00⟩. Build qc with n_steps repeated Trotter steps, each e^{-iJ Z⊗Z dt} followed by e^{-ih X dt} on each qubit, using only rzz and rx. Choose n_steps so that the final state has fidelity at least 0.99 with the exact state e^{-iHt}|00⟩. The circuit may have at most 90 gates.

prediction.question: With a first-order Trotter formula, the norm of the difference between the approximate and the exact final states is about 0.27 for n = 3. What is it about for n = 6?
prediction.explanation: The error of the whole evolution is O(t²/n), so doubling n halves it. The infidelity 1 − F is proportional to the square of this error, so it falls by a factor of 4.

hints: The gate e^{-iθ/2 Z⊗Z} is qc.rzz(θ, 0, 1) and e^{-iθ/2 X} is qc.rx(θ, qubit). To get e^{-iJ Z⊗Z dt}, use θ = 2·J·dt, and θ = 2·h·dt for each X term.
Put the three gates of one step inside for _ in range(n_steps), with dt = t / n_steps already defined. Every step uses the same angles.
Increase n_steps until the fidelity reported by the validator reaches 0.99. The fidelity improves as n grows, and each step costs 3 gates.
